{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''Leslie Hodson''' (born [[Fishlake]] 15 July 1925 – died [[Leeds]] 1 March 2010) was an [[England|English]] physicist<ref name="leeds">{{cite web|url=http://www.leeds.ac.uk/secretariat/obituaries/2010/hodson_leslie.html|title=Obituaries &#124; Secretariat|website=University of Leeds|accessdate=2017-08-28}}</ref> who discovered the [[kaon]] (K+ [[meson]]) sub-atomic particle in 1954.

Hodson was educated at [[Thorne Grammar School]] and the [[University of Manchester]].<ref name="independent">{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/obituaries/leslie-hodson-particle-physicist-and-pioneer-in-the-study-of-cosmic-rays-1983792.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220614/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/obituaries/leslie-hodson-particle-physicist-and-pioneer-in-the-study-of-cosmic-rays-1983792.html |archive-date=14 June 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live|title=Leslie Hodson: Particle physicist and pioneer in the study of cosmic rays|website=The Independent|accessdate=2017-08-28}}</ref> After three years as a research associate at [[Princeton University|Princeton]] he became a [[lecturer]] at the [[University of Leeds]].<ref name="leeds"/> He retired in 1990.
